description:
100 / 1M points as a list of {ts, float}. gorilla_stream 3.0.3: baseline Encoder.encode_elixir(data, []), NIF column NIF.nif_gorilla_encode(data, %{}) (C++ via fine, dirty CPU, precompiled). Compare the full encode job: the kernel builds both bit streams (timestamp delta-of-delta and value XOR) with the bitstring accumulator; headers and CRC32 in Elixir (:erlang.crc32). Agreement: byte-identical output.

Evidence bar (from defk-dtw.4/defk-dtw.15): script examples/<name>.exs with Mix.install of the pinned anchor package; the anchor's Elixir version is the first baseline and must be optimised further in Elixir before the verdict counts (what was tried listed in the header; baseline: :optimized); realistic size declared in the header before any numbers; workload verdict at the realistic size, other size beside; ~6-point geometric sweep with crossover (smallest size where defk >= 2x, or none), skipped if a large run exceeds ~1 min; NIF timing and responsiveness (max and p99 1 ms tick gap, one scheduler, large size, for Elixir/defk/NIF) via Defk.Bench.report/1; Elixir, defk and NIF outputs must agree (failure fails the script); quiet-machine run_all.exs; row added to examples/README.md.

comments.text:
examples/gorilla_encode.exs on branch defk-9p6.16/gorilla-encoding (commit 59dffe2, merge of main a6d9685; mix ci green). PROVISIONAL, measured under load (HLL and defk-8qs agents running); quiet run is defk-sgw.4.

Realistic size (declared in the header): 100-point blocks (Gorilla paper / Prometheus chunk size), timed as 1,000 series x 100 points, one encode call each. Other size: one 1M-point series. Inputs in :persistent_term.

Verdict (DEFK_RESULT gorilla_encode, run_all reads it): Elixir 4.6-5.1 ms vs defk 2.1-2.45 ms: 1.96-2.38x, good in 7 of 8 runs (the 1.96x was best-of-7; now best-of-15). Close to the 2x bar: shared header/CRC32 code (0.27 us/block) and packing the list (~1/3 of defk's 2.1 us) weigh. NIF 5.9-7.2 ms: defk 2.7-2.9x faster (dirty-scheduler hop per call).
1M points (gorilla_encode_1m): Elixir 41.6-44.5 ms vs defk 12.6-14.6 ms: 3.07-3.42x; NIF 31.5-33.3 ms: defk 2.3-2.5x faster. About half of defk's time is packing the list, ~6 ms the kernel.
Sweep (block size 100/630/4k/25k/160k/1M, ~1M points each): 2.25-2.5x, 3.9-4.1x, 4.5-4.7x, 3.5-3.8x, 3.1-3.4x, 2.7-3.3x; crossover 100.
Tick gap (1M points, one scheduler): Elixir max 2.0-2.5 ms, defk 2.2-2.9, NIF 2.0-2.15 (dirty CPU), all at the loaded ~2 ms floor.

Elixir variants (1,000x100 / 1M, ms): encode_elixir 23.6-23.9 / 330-353; one pass with bignum 64-bit patterns 15.1-15.6 / 153-156; halves+tables iolist 16.9-19.3 / ~930; two passes 4.7-4.8 / 40.7-42.6; Gorilla.Elixir (one pass, 32-bit halves, 256-entry zero-count tuples, appended bitstrings; baseline) 4.8-4.9 / 41.6-43.4; word buffer 4.6-5.0 / 40.3-40.8; defk's packed layout 5.3-5.6 / 118-122. Last three within noise.

Agreement: byte-identical (creation time zeroed) across encode_elixir, the 6 variants, the NIF and defk on 53 series (bucket edges, >32-bit deltas, negative/decreasing timestamps, sign flips, -0.0, extremes, ulp steps, integer values, 1M points). Kernel agrees with Elixir mode on 36 cases. Only gorilla_stream-internal disagreement: [] (encode_elixir 80-byte header, NIF <<>>).

Decisions: one kernel builds both streams into one bitstring accumulator, returns {bits, ts_len, val_len}; multi-clause dod_bits helper with masks (gorilla_stream's buckets are one wider than the signed field and wrap); 64-bit XOR bits via x::64-signed and a logical shift on the u64 view instead of the 32-bit-halves split (comment on defk-oit). Pack 4 points per append (1 per append is ~3x slower). The NIF is built from source on OTP 29 (precompiled only for NIF 2.16/2.17), -O2, worked first try.

Filed: defk-cao (needs-triage): a bitstring-returning kernel costs ~0.1 us more per call than a scalar one.
